title: Finite morphisms that are locally finitely presented are finitely presented
statement: Let $p:T\to U$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. If $p$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], then $p$ is of finite presentation: it is quasi-compact and separated (because finite morphisms are affine and separated), and together with local finite presentation this is the definition of finite presentation.

proof.text: By the definition of a finite morphism, $p$ is affine [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Applying the affine-morphism permanence statement [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] gives that $p$ is quasi-compact and separated, hence quasi-separated. The definition of a morphism of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] is local finite presentation together with quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Combining these properties with the hypothesis that $p$ is locally of finite presentation proves that $p$ is of finite presentation.
